title: SDPA backends: restore previous flags and do not treat activation as a speedup
summary: sdpa_kernel enables a named backend subset and restores the previous flags on exit. Flash implementations register without activating.

hardware: CUDA SDPA backends named by this API
conditions: Caller uses scaled_dot_product_attention or a flash impl registry

claims.description: The context manager restores the previous backend set. Its docstring also says exit enables all backends; the implementation is the restore.
register_flash_attention_impl does not activate. activate_flash_attention_impl restores any previous override first. The C++ select_sdp_backend body was not in the inspected headers.

downstream_impact: Serving stacks that wrap SDPA should log the enabled backend and priority rather than assume FLASH_ATTENTION won.
An NPU attention kernel is not implied by this CUDA registry.
recommendations: Treat downstream impact as an InferRSI transfer hypothesis, not a kernel benchmark.
validation_plan: Log current SDPA backends around one forward and compare numerics before any timing run.
limitations: No shape, dtype or mask eligibility was established. No attention benchmark was run.
